title: ECL Trust Policy v1
description: The keys a verifier trusts, the purposes and principal each is trusted for, the interval in which it is trusted, and the revocations the verifier knows. The caller of a verifier supplies it; an evidence bundle never does. Its digest is the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON (RFC 8785 with the ECL number profile).

revocation_policy.description: A revocation policy registered in the vocabulary registry.

keys.description: At most 128 stored keys, allowing selection and rotation. Key identifiers and public keys are each unique; the loader checks that. The reference integrity-policy helper selects at most 64 eligible keys to match its verifier budget.

revocations.description: Each names a key of this policy, and a key is named at most once (the loader checks that in linear time; uniqueItems would compare every pair). A key is revoked for any evaluation time at or after its effective_at. So there are at most as many as there are keys.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC: whole seconds, or three or six fractional digits, then Z. This is the trust-document timestamp profile; signed object timestamps and verifier context parsing follow their own declared profiles.

key_id.description: Names this key in an integrity policy and in an envelope's signature entries.

suite_id.description: An active signature suite of the algorithm-suites registry that this version can carry: ecl.sig.ed25519.v1 or ecl.sig.ecdsa-p256-sha256.v1.

public_key.description: Standard base64 (RFC 4648 section 4, with padding, canonical) of the public key: the raw 32 bytes for ecl.sig.ed25519.v1, or the 65-byte SEC1 uncompressed point (0x04, x, y) for ecl.sig.ecdsa-p256-sha256.v1. The loader checks the length for the suite and, for P-256, that the point is on the curve. One public key belongs to one key_id. For Ed25519 the loader also refuses a value that is not the canonical RFC 8032 encoding of a curve point, and a point of small order (8 times it is the identity), under which a signature made without any private key verifies.

principal.description: The issuer or producer identifier that this key speaks for.

purposes.description: Key purposes allocated in the vocabulary registry (category key_purpose). Each purpose limits the key to the objects of that role.

valid_from.description: The key is trusted from this instant, inclusive.

valid_until.description: The key is trusted until this instant, exclusive. It is later than valid_from. Absent means no end.

effective_at.description: The key is not trusted for any evaluation time at or after this instant.
